transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... it's been happening a lot at the museum. I help out there a bit since I stopped working. We have this big art walk coming up. Actually, the art walk used to be on Thursdays, but they moved it to Saturdays because the downtown businesses complained about the parking. Parking is just a total nightmare down there now since the city put in those new bike lanes. I don't even own a bicycle anymore, my knees just can't take the pedaling, especially on those hills. 

But anyway, what happens is, people at the museum will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’ll be looking right at them, but then I suddenly realize I completely missed the middle of what they said. I end up having to ask them to run it by me again. It's just getting a bit embarrassing.
Is this difficulty paying attention something you have dealt with your whole life, or did it start more recently?

Well, I suppose it's always been there. If I really think back... even in grade school, my report cards always said the exact same things. You know, they'd write "daydreams" or "needs reminders to finish work." They used to handwrite those cards back then, on that thick yellow paper. Mrs. Gable was my third-grade teacher, and she had this beautiful cursive. They don't even teach cursive in schools anymore, which just blows my mind. How are kids supposed to sign a check? Though I guess nobody really writes checks anymore either, do they? Everything is just an app on the phone now. 

But anyway, yeah, my mother actually used to have to sit right beside me at the kitchen table just to keep me on track with my homework. This was before I was twelve, I think. She'd sit there snapping green beans or peeling potatoes for dinner while she watched me. She always bought her produce from this little farm stand out on Route 9, the tomatoes there were just incredible. You can't get tomatoes that taste like that at the supermarket. But yeah, she had to sit right there just so I'd finish my assignments. So it's definitely not a new thing.
Growing up or even now, have you ever had trouble sitting still or felt an inner sense of restlessness?

No, not really. I've never been much of a fidgeter. I can actually sit still for hours, especially if I'm in my favorite recliner. It's this old La-Z-Boy I bought back in, oh, must have been '98, from a Sears that was going out of business at the mall. You know, it's a real shame what happened to Sears. You used to be able to buy absolutely anything from their catalog. I mean, people used to buy whole houses from them! My great-uncle actually lived in a Sears kit house up in Michigan. Had the original hardwood floors and everything. It was a beautiful place, right near a lake where we'd go fishing for bluegill every summer. I haven't been fishing in years, though... the mosquitoes just eat me alive. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, no, I've never really had that restless feeling. I can just sit and watch the birds out the window all afternoon without feeling the need to jump up or move around.
